story.value: The name aluminum comes from the Latin word alumen, alum.
In 1825, the Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted isolated impure aluminum.
The German chemist Friedrich Wöhler first isolated pure aluminum in 1827.

uses.value: Aluminum and aluminum alloys are used to make products such as cans, foils and kitchen utensils.
Aluminum is used in electrical transmission lines because of its light weight.
Aluminum can be deposited on the surface of glass to make mirrors.
Aluminum alloys are important in the construction of modern aircraft and rockets.
